=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:step 0 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The session title is interpolated into a double-quoted shell string. Bash expands `$(...)` (and `${...}`) inside double quotes, so any session title that contains `$(cmd)` will execute `cmd` in the session's shell before the helper runs.
  WHY: The hook consumer (`/implement-plan-claude`, `/implement-issue-claude`, the master poller, the §26.H sweep fixers, and the dispatcher routine) sets the session title; the PR's own implementation log concedes "a session title holding `$(` or a backtick would be expanded inside the double-quoted `session-meta --title "…"` of step 0; chain and dispatcher titles never carry either." That is a runtime invariant, not a code-level guarantee — a PR/issue title containing `$()`, or a future dispatcher that reflects an untrusted field, becomes arbitrary code execution in the very first shell command the session runs. There is no sanitization on the consumer side; `_inline_code` only protects the displayed title, not the one passed to the shell.
- .claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py:113-126 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The detached child inherits the Claude Code session's full environment. The session may carry `GH_TOKEN`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, or other secrets as plain env vars; the child reads only `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` and `CLAUDE_PERMISSION_PROMPT_REPORT`, so the rest is unused but is still in scope for any code path the child executes (urllib, `gh`, future additions).
  WHY: This is a wider attack surface than necessary: a `ReadError` or post-mortem dump of the child would expose the parent's env. A minimal env (`{"PATH": os.environ.get("PATH"), "HOME": os.environ.get("HOME"), REMOTE_SESSION_ENV: ..., REPORT_NOW_SWITCH_ENV: ...}`) would shrink it.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:783-822 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `_filing_lock` is held for the full duration of `_report_to_filing_repo` / `_report_to_own_thread`, which calls `_post` (a `gh api` request with a 60s timeout). Other reporters and `file` calls against the same log directory queue behind that.
  WHY: This is intentional (the lock guarantees the reservation-then-POST-then-finalise sequence is atomic against the same `immediate-state.json`), but under a burst — multiple PRs in a `claude-pr-catch-all` sweep, or a swarm of new sessions reporting their first prompts — they serialise on the HTTP round-trip, not on the lock itself. The on-disk save is fast; the POST is the slow part.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:830-836 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `_release_reservation` mutates the in-memory bucket (`pop`, decrement count) and then tries to save with `contextlib.suppress(OSError)`. If the save raises any OSError (disk full, read-only mount, broken pipe on the write), the on-disk state still carries the `pending` reservation.
  WHY: The next `_report_now` call for the same session reloads state, sees `sig in bucket["reports"]`, and returns "skipped: already reported" — even though no POST ever landed. The pattern is then filed at step 14 (`_file_pending` ignores `pending`, which is correct), but the immediate report is lost. The dual-failure window (reservation save succeeded, release save failed) is narrow but real on a full disk.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:1021-1027 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: An `OSError` from `mkdir` is reported with `{"ok": False, "error": str(exc)}`, but a subsequent `_run_session_meta` call from a different cwd (or after a transient failure) would still find the same error. There is no retry, no metric, no log line.
  WHY: A user's home directory being read-only at one moment would silently turn every step-0 session-meta call into a no-op report (`not recorded` forever, even when the FS recovers). Low severity but worth a `::warning::` log so the operator sees it once.
- .claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py:113-126 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The hook now starts a detached child on every `PermissionRequest`. The child is gated by `REPORTER_PATH.is_file()`, a kill switch env var, and an attendance check inside the child, but the hook itself has no documented kill switch and no per-prompt throttle.
  WHY: Today the helper exits 0 silently and the child does at most one POST per signature per session. The hook is the single chokepoint — if a future change inside `report-now` forgets the `pending` reservation, the child's per-session `count` cap (5) is the only thing standing between a runaway hook and a flood of GitHub API calls. Worth documenting the hook-level guard in `.claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py` (e.g. an `if not _report_now_enabled(): return` short-circuit so the kill switch is honoured even if the child is unreachable) so the guard is colocated with the spawn site.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
